fix_commit_message:
[sfnt] Avoid allocation bomb in compressed SVG documents.

Reported as

  https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/416538625

* src/sfnt/ttsvg.c (MAX_SVG_SIZE): New macro.
  (tt_face_load_svg_doc): Reject too large buffer.
agent_reasoning: The introduced feature wires the previously-dormant SVG document loader (`tt_face_load_svg_doc` in src/sfnt/ttsvg.c) into the public TrueType and CFF glyph-loading paths. That loader trusts the gzip trailer's 4-byte ISIZE field as the exact size to FT_QALLOC for the decompression buffer, with no upper bound. A malicious OT-SVG font can set ISIZE to a huge value (close to 2^32) to force a massive allocation attempt (an "allocation bomb"), which can exhaust memory or abort the process — a denial-of-service reachable purely by loading a glyph, as flagged by OSS-Fuzz issue 416538625. The on-disk fix adds a `MAX_SVG_SIZE` cap (1<<26, 64MiB) and rejects the document with `Array_Too_Large` before allocating when the claimed uncompressed size meets or exceeds that cap, matching the upstream fix commit while keeping the newly-introduced glyph-loading call sites untouched.
